coronary.seoTitle: Coronary artery disease care in Tampa
coronary.intro: Coronary artery disease happens when plaque builds up inside the arteries that supply the heart muscle. Narrowed arteries can limit blood flow during activity, and a plaque that ruptures can cause a heart attack. Early evaluation and steady treatment lower that risk.
symptoms: Chest pain, pressure, or tightness, especially with exertion or stress
Shortness of breath during activity that used to be easy
Pain that spreads to the arm, jaw, neck, or back
Unusual fatigue, nausea, or sweating with effort
No symptoms at all, with disease found on a test or after a heart attack
evaluation: A review of symptoms, family history, and risk factors such as blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, and smoking
An electrocardiogram (ECG) and blood tests
Stress testing or imaging, such as an echocardiogram or a coronary CT scan, when appropriate
Cardiac catheterization in a hospital when other results point to a significant blockage
treatment: Medications that lower cholesterol, control blood pressure, prevent clots, and relieve chest pain
Lifestyle changes, including diet, activity, and stopping smoking
Coronary stenting (PCI) to open a narrowed artery, performed in a hospital catheterization lab
Referral for bypass surgery when it is the better option

heart-failure.seoTitle: Advanced heart failure care in Tampa
heart-failure.intro: Heart failure means the heart is not pumping or filling as well as the body needs. It does not mean the heart has stopped. With the right medications and close follow-up, many people feel better, stay out of the hospital, and live longer.
symptoms: Shortness of breath with activity or when lying flat
Swelling in the legs, ankles, or abdomen
Rapid weight gain from fluid
Fatigue and reduced ability to exercise
Waking at night short of breath
evaluation: An echocardiogram to measure how well the heart pumps and how the valves work
Blood tests, including kidney function and markers of heart strain
A search for the cause, such as blocked arteries, valve disease, high blood pressure, or a weakened heart muscle
Regular review of weight, symptoms, and medications
treatment: Guideline-directed medications that strengthen the heart over time and reduce hospital stays
Diuretics to remove extra fluid
Treating the underlying cause, such as a blocked artery or a valve problem
Advanced therapies, devices, or transplant evaluation for heart failure that does not respond to standard care

structural.seoTitle: Heart valve and structural heart disease care in Tampa
structural.intro: Structural heart disease covers problems with the heart's valves, walls, and chambers. Many can now be treated through a catheter placed in a blood vessel, without open-heart surgery, which often means a shorter recovery.
symptoms: A heart murmur found during an exam
Shortness of breath, fatigue, or reduced stamina
Chest discomfort, dizziness, or fainting with exertion
Swelling in the legs
A stroke or mini-stroke that may be linked to a hole in the heart or to atrial fibrillation
evaluation: An echocardiogram, sometimes including a transesophageal echo for a closer view
Cardiac CT to measure the valve and plan any procedure
A review of overall health to weigh catheter-based treatment against surgery
treatment: Monitoring for valve disease that is mild and not causing symptoms
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) for a narrowed aortic valve
Transcatheter mitral repair (MitraClip) for a leaking mitral valve
ASD/PFO closure, and left atrial appendage closure (Watchman) to lower stroke risk in atrial fibrillation when blood thinners are a problem
Procedures are performed in a hospital, with evaluation and follow-up in the office

imaging.seoTitle: Cardiac imaging: echocardiography and cardiac CT in Tampa
imaging.intro: Cardiac imaging shows the heart's structure and function without surgery. The results guide diagnosis, help decide whether a procedure is needed, and plan it when it is.
symptoms: A murmur, abnormal ECG, or symptoms that need a closer look
Known valve disease or heart failure that needs monitoring
Risk factors that call for a check of the coronary arteries
Planning for a structural heart procedure such as TAVR
evaluation: Echocardiography (heart ultrasound) to see the chambers, valves, and pumping strength
Stress echocardiography to see how the heart responds to exercise
Transesophageal echocardiography for detailed views of the valves
Coronary CT angiography and calcium scoring to look for plaque in the arteries
treatment: Imaging results are reviewed with you and used to shape the treatment plan
Repeat imaging tracks changes over time
Where each test is performed is confirmed when it is ordered

prevention.seoTitle: Cholesterol and heart disease prevention in Tampa
prevention.intro: Most heart attacks and strokes come from plaque that builds up over years. Lowering cholesterol and managing other risk factors early can slow that process and prevent a first event.
symptoms: High LDL cholesterol or triglycerides on blood work
A family history of early heart disease
High blood pressure, diabetes, or smoking
Inherited cholesterol conditions, such as familial hypercholesterolemia or high lipoprotein(a)
A coronary calcium score that shows plaque
evaluation: A full lipid panel and, when useful, advanced tests such as lipoprotein(a)
A calculation of your 10-year cardiovascular risk
Coronary calcium scoring when it would change the treatment decision
treatment: A plan for diet, activity, weight, and blood pressure
Statins and other cholesterol-lowering medications, including newer options when statins are not enough or not tolerated
Regular follow-up to reach and keep your targets

shock.seoTitle: Cardiogenic shock and mechanical circulatory support
shock.intro: Cardiogenic shock is an emergency in which the heart suddenly cannot pump enough blood to the body, most often after a large heart attack. It is treated in the hospital, sometimes with a temporary heart pump that supports the circulation while the heart recovers.
symptoms: Severe shortness of breath and low blood pressure
Confusion, cold or clammy skin, and low urine output
It usually follows a heart attack or severe heart failure. Call 911 for these symptoms.
evaluation: Emergency assessment in the hospital, including ECG, echocardiogram, and blood tests
Cardiac catheterization to find and treat a blocked artery
treatment: Opening the blocked artery as quickly as possible
Temporary mechanical support such as the Impella heart pump during high-risk procedures or recovery
Intensive care and medications to support blood pressure
Follow-up in the office after discharge
